description: Alpine updates. (1) apk pins (built-in `apk` datasource, extracted by the dockerfile manager from `RUN apk add` since Renovate 44.96.0): ALL non-major apk bumps (patch/pin/digest/minor) share ONE 'alpine packages' group so they open a single mutually-buildable PR — Alpine repos keep only the latest build of each apk and purge older ones from the index, so a Dockerfile pinning a drifted version fails to build; splitting apk bumps across PRs deadlocks (each PR still pins the purged versions the other bumps). No soak, run any time, and automerged once CI (the real Docker build — the exact check a stale pin would fail) passes. separateMinorPatch/separateMajorMinor are forced false for the apk datasource so no apk bump ever splits onto its own branch, and rangeStrategy is forced to 'replace' (see that rule — without it every drifted pin goes silently dark). The consumer supplies the registryUrls that name its Alpine release line; this preset stays version-agnostic. (2) Alpine base image (docker datasource): minor bumps cross release lines and require hand-editing that consumer-side registryUrls branch — so they are gated to manual review; patch base bumps stay in-line and automerge via docker.json's bundle. (3) node image bumps (minor/patch) are gated to manual review: node:*-alpine carries an Alpine release line that nothing else gates. Extend AFTER automerge.json and docker.json. Major bumps fall through to default.json's manual-review rule.

packageRules.description: Force rangeStrategy 'replace' for every apk lookup. default.json sets a top-level `rangeStrategy: pin`, and the dockerfile manager SUPPORTS pin (it pins base-image digests), so apk deps inherit it — unlike the old custom.regex manager, which does not support pin and silently fell back to replace. That inheritance is fatal here: an APKINDEX carries ONLY the newest build of each package, so a pin that has already drifted is absent from the release list; getCurrentVersion's 'pin' branch then returns getSatisfyingVersion([], currentValue) => null, Renovate logs 'No currentVersion or lockedVersion found' and sets skipReason 'invalid-value', and the package produces NO update — exactly the drifted pins that most need one go dark with no warning and no Dependency Dashboard entry. Only the 'replace' branch reaches the `isVersion(currentValue) => currentValue` fallback that makes a drifted pin updatable. Measured on 44.97.1: with pin, nut-cgi's stale curl and openssl pins produced nothing; with replace, they produce the same 8.22.0-r0 / 3.5.8-r0 bumps the retired custom.alpine datasource did. Do NOT remove this, and do NOT scope it by updateType. ignoreUnstable is set explicitly for the same belt-and-braces reason: ~0.3% of Alpine apks carry _rc/_alpha/~beta builds, apk versioning correctly reports those unstable (loose did not), and this keeps them out of the automerged group even if a consumer flips the global default.

Alpine apk non-major pins (patch/pin/digest/minor): ONE group, skip the soak, run off-schedule, automerge. Formerly split into 'alpine packages' (patch/pin/digest, automerge) + 'alpine packages (minor)' (manual) — that opened two PRs in any window where one package drifted patch and another drifted minor, and BOTH failed CI because each still pinned the purged versions the other PR bumped. Deadlock. Unified into one group so every drifted apk pin co-bumps in a single PR that automerges once CI passes. Automerge is safe HERE precisely because unifying the group makes the PR self-consistent — CI runs the real Docker build, which is the exact check that would fail on a stale pin. This rule ALSO peels apk pins back out of docker.json's 'dockerfile bases' group: that rule matches `matchManagers: [dockerfile]` with no datasource filter, and apk deps now come from the dockerfile manager, so without this preset extended AFTER docker.json every apk pin would ride the base-image group instead. Do NOT re-split by update type to isolate minor bumps for review — that re-introduces the deadlock.

Node runtime images carry an Alpine release line (node:24.19.0-alpine is Alpine 3.24.1), and Node moves that base at its own cadence — including on patch rebuilds. A crossing invalidates the consumer's apk `registryUrls` branch (v3.24 -> v3.25), which is the one place the release line is written. Gate every node image bump to manual review so a human checks the resulting line. Deliberately sets NO groupName: node.json's toolchain-versions group must keep node and pnpm co-bumping in ONE PR, and a group here would split them — the gate still works because a single automerge:false upgrade disables the whole branch and addLabels is unioned across upgrades. Majors already carry needs-review via docker.json's runtime rule. digest/pinDigest are EXCLUDED — a known, accepted gap: a same-tag rebuild can re-point the floating node:*-alpine alias at a new Alpine line. Pinning node:X-alpine3.24 instead was REJECTED: Renovate cannot couple the node version and the Alpine suffix, so an explicit suffix would freeze the line with nothing ever signalling the move to 3.25 — trading a rare silent crossing for a permanent silent stall. Gating digests was rejected on automerge cost (pinDigests is on, so digest refreshes are frequent). This rule is UNCONDITIONAL for every :alpine consumer, and is the THIRD place node/docker.io/library/node is named across these presets — keep it in sync with node.json's toolchain-versions and docker.json's dockerfile-bases negation list.

Alpine base image (docker datasource) minor bumps cross release lines, which requires hand-editing the `branch=vX.Y` in the consumer's apk registryUrls. Gate ONLY these to manual review; never automerge. Patch bumps and digest-only rebuilds stay within the line (registryUrls still valid) and ride docker.json's 'dockerfile bases' group + automerge.json's non-major bundle.
